key_insight: HPRO improves emotional text-to-speech by optimizing preferences in a staged, hierarchical way instead of forcing one shared latent space to learn everything at once. This reduces conflict between content and emotion, helping models produce more expressive and controllable speech.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the limitation of supervised fine-tuning in LLM-based TTS, which often produces average, less emotional prosody. It also tackles two structural mismatches in preference optimization: information conflict between content and emotion, and reward imbalance that can weaken emotional learning.
method: Introduces Hierarchical Progressive Reward Optimization (HPRO), a preference-based training strategy for emotional TTS.
Uses preference extraction to separate and better align content-related and emotion-related learning signals.
Applies progressive, hierarchical reward optimization to reduce gradient conflicts and improve expressive prosody generation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work offers a more robust way to train emotionally expressive TTS systems without collapsing into bland average speech. It may also inspire similar hierarchical preference-optimization strategies for other generative models with competing objectives.

paper_title: HPRO: Hierarchical Progressive Reward Optimization via Preference Extraction for Emotional Text-to-Speech
paper_authors: Sihang Nie, Xiaofen Xing, Rui Xing, Haoming Li, Ruitong Xiao
